title: voxelRemesh
body:
## voxelRemesh

Rebuilds a copy of the input mesh as a new surface from a voxelised volume using Blender's Remesh modifier in Voxel mode. The result is a single quad-dominant surface; overlapping joined parts fuse into one shell (a 'voxel union') and features smaller than voxelSize are lost. Schemaxis first rejects requests whose estimated bounding grid exceeds 8 million cells (RESOURCE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED).

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- voxelSize is in the input's local units; on a scaled object (cube size, transform scale) the world voxel size differs. Use applyTransform first.
- The input should enclose a volume; open sheets produce thin or unexpected shells.
- Topology, vertex count and fine detail change; do not use the result for dimensional checks finer than the voxel size.

Native binding: `voxelRemesh`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | one node | yes | `data` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `voxelSize` | Edge length of the voxels used to rebuild the surface (Blender voxel_size, object space). Smaller voxels keep finer detail but cost memory and time roughly with the cube of 1/voxelSize; Schemaxis rejects sizes whose estimated bounding grid exceeds 8 million cells. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"exclusiveMinimum":true}` | `0.1` |
| `adaptivity` | Native face reduction after remeshing: 0 keeps uniform quads; larger values simplify flat regions into larger triangles (and disable Blender's pole fixing). | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1}` | `0` |
